title: Promoter Methylation of Tumor-Suppressor Genes and Thyroid Cancer Risk: A Meta-Analysis Protocol
author: Fatemeh Khatami
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.i9zch76

steps.title: Screen and Select Studies
steps.instruction: Review nominated studies independently by two authors to identify those reporting gene promoter methylation in thyroid cancer tumor tissue (fresh-frozen, FFPE, or plasma) compared to sex- and age-matched controls.

substeps.instruction: Define normal controls as similar tissue types, including normal adjacent tissue of thyroid cancer (NPTC), goiter, and nodular goiter (NG) samples.
Exclude studies with insufficient data, even after contacting the author.

steps.title: Extract Study Data
steps.instruction: Extract the following specific information from each included study into tables:

substeps.instruction: General info: first author, year of publication, and country of research.
Sample details: type of sample, type of tissue (tumor and control), and pathological stage.
Technical details: method for methylation determination and name of targeted gene(s).
Results: frequency of promoter methylation in target gene(s) for both tumor and normal thyroid tissues.

steps.title: Assess Study Quality
steps.instruction: Evaluate the quality of each individual study using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) assessment tool.

substeps.instruction: Score case-control studies based on selection, comparability, and exposure.

steps.title: Perform Statistical Analysis
steps.instruction: Use Stata 12.0 to evaluate the association between promoter methylation of the eight TSGs and thyroid cancer risk using odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

substeps.instruction: Pool study-specific OR, sensitivity, and specificity estimates using a fixed-effects model if no significant heterogeneity exists; otherwise, use a random-effects model.
Check heterogeneity using chi-squared and I-squared tests (significant if p=0.10 and/or I2 > 50%).

Perform sub-group analysis and meta-regression to evaluate sources of heterogeneity, including study design (prospective/retrospective, year), population characteristics (gender, ethnicity, age, disease types, stage), test characteristics, and reference standard versions.
Use the likelihood ratio test to determine the statistical significance of covariates in the bivariate or Rutter and Gatsonis HSROC models.
Conduct sensitivity analysis by ignoring one study at a time to measure the effect of single studies on the overall estimate.

steps.title: Assess Publication Bias
steps.instruction: Evaluate the potential for publication bias using multiple statistical methods.

substeps.instruction: Generate funnel plots (plotting study results against precision).
Apply the Begg rank correlation method, Egger weighted regression method, and the trim-and-fill method.

steps.title: Synthesize and Present Results
steps.instruction: Organize the synthesized data into two separate tables and graphical displays.

substeps.instruction: Create one table for study quality based on the Newcastle-Ottawa Quality Assessment Form.
Create a second table for study design, participants, test characteristics, and results.
Extract test characteristics into 2 x 2 tables.
Display study-specific sensitivity and specificity estimations with 95% CIs in forest plots using Review Manager (Version 5.2).
